extraction: Verbatim transcription of published Table 1. Row count asserted = 16. No unit conversion, no derivation.
note: IMPORTANT SCOPE LIMIT: dV20 is a GLOBAL, SPATIALLY UNRESOLVED single-dish HI linewidth. In classic PRGs the HI is associated with the POLAR structure, so dV20 traces the POLAR plane, NOT the host disk. This table therefore contains ONE plane only. The paper DOES derive host-plane velocities, but only for five systems and only in a figure: it states it computed log(dV) for the host galaxies of NGC 4650A, NGC 660, NGC 2685, UGC 7576 and A0136-0801 'using optical absorption-line rotation curves along the host galaxy equatorial plane' (sources: Sackett et al. 1994; van Driel et al. 1995; Simien & Prugniel 1997; Whitmore et al. 1990; Schweizer et al. 1983), and plots them as large crosses with an arrow to the ring value in its S0 Tully-Fisher figure (iodicee_fig8.ps). Those five host-plane velocities are NOT tabulated anywhere in the paper. For NGC 4650A the host circular velocity was obtained from the stellar rotation and velocity dispersion of Combes & Arnaboldi 1996 by converting to an equivalent gas linewidth assuming a 10 km/s dispersion. M_B for NGC 4650A is from Gallagher et al. 2002; for NGC 2586 and A0136-0801 the B magnitudes relative to the host galaxy are from Reshetnikov et al. 1994. For NGC 660 the velocities are derived from Halpha data (van Driel et al. 1995).
